components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; recognising something is naming it.
人 (rén) gives the exact sound, and also means "person".
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家 home, 安 safe, 客 guest; settling down under a roof.
正 (zhèng, upright; the lower part is written 疋) is a loose sound clue for dìng; also in 证 zhèng and 政 zhèng.

example.hanzi: 警方认定这起事故是人为操作失误造成的。
example.pinyin: jǐngfāng rèndìng zhè qǐ shìgù shì rénwéi cāozuò shīwù zàochéng de.
example.english: Police determined that the accident was caused by human operational error.
example.fact: The 1986 Chernobyl disaster was ultimately attributed by investigators to a combination of a flawed reactor design and operator error during a poorly planned safety test, when staff disabled key safety systems. The explosion released radioactive material equivalent to hundreds of times more fallout than the atomic bombs dropped on Hiroshima and Nagasaki combined.

examples.hanzi: 大家都认定他是这次比赛的冠军。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu rèndìng tā shì zhè cì bǐsài de guànjūn.
examples.english: Everyone is convinced that he's the champion of this match.

examples.hanzi: 我认定这个办法是对的,不会改。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ rèndìng zhège bànfǎ shì duì de, bú huì gǎi.
examples.english: I'm sure this method is right and won't change it.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 讠 is the simplified 言 (speech), as in 说, 话, 读; 语 is language and spoken words.
吾 (wú) — loose hint — 语 is yǔ; 吾 also sounds out 悟 wù.
气 (air, vapor) — lines of rising vapor or breath. Add water for 汽 steam; seen in 生气 get angry, 空气 air.

example.hanzi: 她说话的语气突然变得严肃起来。
example.pinyin: tā shuōhuà de yǔqì tūrán biàn de yánsù qǐlái.
example.english: Her tone suddenly became serious.
example.fact: Researchers estimate that in face-to-face communication, tone of voice and body language often carry more emotional meaning than the actual words spoken, a finding popularly (if often oversimplified) traced to psychologist Albert Mehrabian's 1967 studies on how people judge feelings like liking or disliking.

examples.hanzi: 你别用这种语气跟我说话。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bié yòng zhè zhǒng yǔqì gēn wǒ shuōhuà.
examples.english: Don't talk to me in that tone.

examples.hanzi: 从他的语气里,我听出他不太高兴。
examples.pinyin: Cóng tā de yǔqì lǐ, wǒ tīngchū tā bú tài gāoxìng.
examples.english: From his tone, I could tell he wasn't very happy.

components.note: 此 (cǐ) is a sound clue for 紫 zǐ, 雌 cí and 些 xiē; as a word it means "this".
日 (sun) — day and time, as in 晴 clear, 早 early, 明 bright; time was read from the sun.
寸 (cùn) stands in for 寺 sì in the traditional 時; sound clue is loose. 寺 also gives 诗 shī and 持 chí.

example.hanzi: 此时，太阳正缓缓落下。
example.pinyin: cǐshí, tàiyáng zhèng huǎnhuǎn luòxià.
example.english: At this moment, the sun was slowly setting.
example.fact: A sunset's colors appear because sunlight travels through more atmosphere at a low angle, scattering away most of the blue and violet wavelengths and leaving the reds and oranges to reach our eyes — the same physical process, called Rayleigh scattering, that makes the daytime sky blue in the first place.

examples.hanzi: 此时此刻,我只想回家休息。
examples.pinyin: Cǐshí cǐkè, wǒ zhǐ xiǎng huíjiā xiūxi.
examples.english: At this very moment, I just want to go home and rest.

examples.hanzi: 此时的他已经走远了。
examples.pinyin: Cǐshí de tā yǐjīng zǒu yuǎn le.
examples.english: By then he had already walked far away.

components.note: 隹 (zhuī, short-tailed bird) — 难 was first the name of a bird; "hard" is a borrowed use. The 又 here stands in for the traditional left part.
心 (heart) — feelings and thinking: 想 think, 思, 感 feel, 忙; forgetting is a loss of the heart's hold.
亡 (wáng, lose) gives the sound and fits the sense: to lose from the mind.

example.hanzi: 这是我一生中最难忘的旅行。
example.pinyin: zhè shì wǒ yīshēng zhōng zuì nánwàng de lǚxíng.
example.english: This was the most unforgettable trip of my life.
example.fact: People with highly superior autobiographical memory, a rare condition studied since the mid-2000s, can recall the exact day of the week and personal details for almost every date of their lives, yet brain scans show their memory for unrelated facts, like memorizing random lists, is entirely ordinary.

examples.hanzi: 那个夏天的海边之旅让我难忘。
examples.pinyin: Nàge xiàtiān de hǎibiān zhī lǚ ràng wǒ nánwàng.
examples.english: That summer trip to the seaside is unforgettable for me.

examples.hanzi: 老师的这句话让我终身难忘。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī de zhè jù huà ràng wǒ zhōngshēn nánwàng.
examples.english: This sentence from my teacher is something I'll never forget.

components.note: 工 (work) — a left hand 𠂇 with 工 (work): the hand that helps with work; compare 右 on the right.
手 (hand) — a picture of a hand with fingers spread. As a left-hand radical it becomes 扌 in 打 hit, 拿 take, 推 push.

example.hanzi: 他习惯用左手写字。
example.pinyin: tā xíguàn yòng zuǒshǒu xiězì.
example.english: He is used to writing with his left hand.
example.fact: Left-handed people make up only about 10 percent of the global population, a ratio that has stayed remarkably stable across cultures and centuries. Studies of cave art and ancient tools suggest this same roughly one-in-ten split existed among prehistoric humans tens of thousands of years ago.

examples.hanzi: 我是右撇子,可是我弟弟用左手吃饭。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ shì yòupiězi, kěshì wǒ dìdi yòng zuǒshǒu chīfàn.
examples.english: I'm right-handed, but my younger brother eats with his left hand.

examples.hanzi: 请看你的左手边,那里就是出口。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng kàn nǐ de zuǒshǒu biān, nàlǐ jiù shì chūkǒu.
examples.english: Please look to your left; the exit is right there.

components.note: 大 (big person) — a person with a line above the head, marking the sky above; tiān = heaven, sky, day.
大 (big person) — a person with a line above the head, marking the sky above; tiān = heaven, sky, day.

example.hanzi: 他天天早上都去公园跑步。
example.pinyin: tā tiāntiān zǎoshang dōu qù gōngyuán pǎobù.
example.english: He goes jogging in the park every morning.
example.fact: Marathon monks of Mount Hiei in Japan undertake a thousand-day challenge in which they run roughly 40 kilometers a day for 100 consecutive days each year, spread over seven years, as an extreme Buddhist practice of physical discipline meant to achieve spiritual enlightenment through repetition.

examples.hanzi: 我天天坐地铁上班。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ tiāntiān zuò dìtiě shàngbān.
examples.english: I take the subway to work every day.

examples.hanzi: 她天天都给奶奶打电话。
examples.pinyin: Tā tiāntiān dōu gěi nǎinai dǎ diànhuà.
examples.english: She calls her grandma every day.

meanings: (of a product, service, project etc) flagship

components.note: 手 (hand) — marks the hand and its actions, as in 拿, 掌 palm, 摩; 拳 is the fist, a hand curled up.
龹 (a curling shape) hints at the sound: 拳 quán is close to 卷 juǎn and 圈 quān.
页 (head, page) — in traditional 頭 (豆 + 页): 页 is an old picture of a head, as in 顶, 领, 额. 头 dropped both parts.
大 (big) — the bottom. Memory aid: a big 大 body with two dots ⺀ like eyes above — the head, as in 头发. The dictionary's reading is loose.

example.hanzi: 他紧紧地握着拳头，努力控制自己的情绪。
example.pinyin: tā jǐnjǐn de wòzhe quántou, nǔlì kòngzhì zìjǐ de qíngxù.
example.english: He clenched his fist tightly, trying to control his emotions.
example.fact: The mantis shrimp can snap its clawed forelimb so fast that it creates cavitation bubbles in the water, generating a brief flash of light and heat nearly as hot as the sun's surface, and the resulting shockwave can crack aquarium glass or shatter a snail shell in a single strike.

examples.hanzi: 小男孩握紧拳头,想打赢那场架。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo nánhái wòjǐn quántou, xiǎng dǎyíng nà chǎng jià.
examples.english: The little boy clenched his fists, wanting to win the fight.

examples.hanzi: 他的拳头比我的大一倍。
examples.pinyin: Tā de quántou bǐ wǒ de dà yí bèi.
examples.english: His fist is twice as big as mine.

components.note: 石 (stone) — 石 as in 破 break, 砖 brick: hard things colliding — 碰 is to bump into.
並 (bìng) — loose hint — 碰 is pèng; 並 (bìng) also sounds out 拼 pīn and 屏 píng.
上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.

example.hanzi: 我在路上碰上了一个老朋友。
example.pinyin: wǒ zài lùshàng pèngshàng le yī gè lǎo péngyou.
example.english: I ran into an old friend on the road.
example.fact: Voyager 1, launched in 1977, unexpectedly encountered a region of dense interstellar plasma in 2012 as it crossed into interstellar space, a discovery that only happened because the spacecraft's instruments recorded oscillations after a coronal mass ejection from the sun reached it a year later, letting scientists measure the plasma density directly.

examples.hanzi: 我出门买菜时,碰上了邻居。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ chūmén mǎicài shí, pèngshàngle línjū.
examples.english: I ran into my neighbor when I went out to buy groceries.

examples.hanzi: 今天真倒霉,又碰上堵车。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān zhēn dǎoméi, yòu pèngshàng dǔchē.
examples.english: Such bad luck today, I ran into a traffic jam again.

components.note: 氵 (water, 三点水) — marks water and liquids, as in 海 sea, 河 river, 汤 soup; 灌 is pouring water to irrigate.
雚 (guàn) — same sound: 灌 guàn. 雚 also sounds out 罐 guàn and 观 guān.

example.hanzi: 农民在给田地灌水。
example.pinyin: Nóngmín zài gěi tiándì guàn shuǐ.
example.english: The farmers are irrigating the fields.
example.fact: 灌 builds 灌溉 (irrigation) and 灌输 (to instill). On forums, 灌水 means to post filler. 灌饼 is a Chinese breakfast flatbread filled with egg, and 灌篮 is a basketball slam dunk.

examples.hanzi: 请往瓶子里灌满开水。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng wǎng píngzi lǐ guàn mǎn kāishuǐ.
examples.english: Please fill the bottle with boiling water.

examples.hanzi: 他把音乐灌进了耳朵里。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ yīnyuè guàn jìn le ěrduo lǐ.
examples.english: He poured the music into his ears.

components.note: 氵 (water, 三点水) — marks water and liquids, as in 海 sea, 河 river, 汤 soup; 添 is adding more, as water is topped up.
忝 (tiǎn) — close sound: 添 tiān. 忝 also sounds out 舔 tiǎn.

example.hanzi: 请再给我添一碗饭。
example.pinyin: Qǐng zài gěi wǒ tiān yì wǎn fàn.
example.english: Please give me another bowl of rice.
example.fact: 添 means to add or refill: 添饭, 添加 (to add), 增添. 添麻烦 (to cause trouble) is a staple of politeness: 给您添麻烦了, "sorry for the trouble."

examples.hanzi: 你要不要再添一点汤？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yào bu yào zài tiān yìdiǎn tāng?
examples.english: Would you like to add some more soup?

examples.hanzi: 家里添了一个小宝宝。
examples.pinyin: Jiālǐ tiān le yí ge xiǎo bǎobao.
examples.english: A new baby has joined the family.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical — 握 is to grasp, as in 握手 handshake.
屋 (wū) — near sound — 握 is wò; 屋 also sounds out 幄 wò.
手 (hand) — a picture of a hand with fingers spread. As a left-hand radical it becomes 扌 in 打 hit, 拿 take, 推 push.

example.hanzi: 两位领导人在会议开始前握手致意。
example.pinyin: liǎng wèi lǐngdǎorén zài huìyì kāishǐ qián wòshǒu zhìyì.
example.english: The two leaders shook hands before the meeting began.
example.fact: The handshake is believed to have originated as a way to show one was not carrying a weapon, and the up-and-down shaking motion may have started as a check to dislodge any hidden blade from a sleeve — a practical gesture of trust that evolved into today's social greeting.

examples.hanzi: 见面时,他热情地跟我握手。
examples.pinyin: Jiànmiàn shí, tā rèqíng de gēn wǒ wòshǒu.
examples.english: When we met, he shook hands with me warmly.

examples.hanzi: 两队球员比赛后互相握手。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng duì qiúyuán bǐsài hòu hùxiāng wòshǒu.
examples.english: The players of the two teams shook hands after the match.

components.note: 讠 (speech, simplified 言) — speech and talking: 说, 计, 谈; 设 is to set up or plan by instruction.
殳 (shū, hand holding a tool) is only a loose sound clue; also in 投 tóu and 股 gǔ.
方 (square; flag) — stands in for the flag part 㫃 of the old form, as in 旗 flag, 旅 travel, 族 clan; the meaning 'bestow, carry out' came later.
㐌 (looks like 也 plus a stroke) — traditionally the sound part (也 yě); today the match with shī is only a loose clue.

example.hanzi: 这所学校的体育设施非常齐全。
example.pinyin: zhè suǒ xuéxiào de tǐyù shèshī fēicháng qíquán.
example.english: This school's sports facilities are very well equipped.
example.fact: The International Space Station, humanity's largest inhabited facility in orbit, took over a decade to assemble from 1998 to 2011 using more than 30 missions, and it travels around Earth roughly every 90 minutes, meaning astronauts on board witness about 16 sunrises and sunsets each day.

examples.hanzi: 我们小区的娱乐设施很完整。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xiǎoqū de yúlè shèshī hěn wánzhěng.
examples.english: The recreation facilities in our neighborhood are very complete.

examples.hanzi: 这座城市的公共设施越来越好。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò chéngshì de gōnggòng shèshī yuè lái yuè hǎo.
examples.english: This city's public facilities are getting better and better.

components.note: 田 (field) — traditional 奮 shows a bird 隹 spreading its wings 大 out of a field: bursting into effort.
斗 (dipper) — a measuring dipper with a handle; as a radical it marks measuring: 料, 科, 斜. Also read dǒu (a measure) or dòu (to fight).

example.hanzi: 他为了实现自己的梦想不断奋斗。
example.pinyin: tā wèile shíxiàn zìjǐ de mèngxiǎng bùduàn fèndòu.
example.english: He kept striving to achieve his dream.
example.fact: Thomas Edison and his team reportedly tested thousands of different filament materials before settling on a carbonized bamboo fiber that let his light bulb burn for over 1,200 hours, an extreme case of trial-and-error persistence that Edison summarized in his famous remark that genius is one percent inspiration and ninety-nine percent perspiration.

examples.hanzi: 为了更好的生活,他们每天努力奋斗。
examples.pinyin: Wèile gèng hǎo de shēnghuó, tāmen měitiān nǔlì fèndòu.
examples.english: They strive every day for a better life.

examples.hanzi: 这是我们共同奋斗得来的成绩。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒmen gòngtóng fèndòu délái de chéngjì.
examples.english: This is an achievement we earned by striving together.

components.note: 隹 (zhuī, short-tailed bird) — 难 was first the name of a bird; "hard" is a borrowed use. The 又 here stands in for the traditional left part.
广 (building) — 广 is a building radical, as in 店, 床; 度 also sounds out 渡 dù and 镀 dù.

example.hanzi: 这道数学题的难度比想象中要大。
example.pinyin: zhè dào shùxué tí de nándù bǐ xiǎngxiàng zhōng yào dà.
example.english: This math problem is more difficult than expected.
example.fact: The Collatz conjecture, a math problem so simple a child can state it — take any positive number, and if it's even halve it, if odd triple it and add one, repeat — has resisted proof since the 1930s despite being verified by computer for every number up to nearly 2^68, illustrating that a problem's simplicity says nothing about its true difficulty.

examples.hanzi: 这个游戏的难度太高,我通不了关。
examples.pinyin: Zhège yóuxì de nándù tài gāo, wǒ tōng bù liǎo guān.
examples.english: This game is too hard and I can't clear the level.

examples.hanzi: 你可以根据自己的水平选择难度。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ gēnjù zìjǐ de shuǐpíng xuǎnzé nándù.
examples.english: You can pick a difficulty level based on your ability.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 推 push, 拉 pull; 抵 is to push against.
氐 (dī) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 低 dī and 底 dǐ.
辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过, 进, 送; 达 is to get through to, to reach.
大 (dà) is only a loose stand-in for the old sound part, so treat it as a rough clue for dá.

example.hanzi: 飞机将于晚上八点抵达机场。
example.pinyin: fēijī jiāng yú wǎnshàng bā diǎn dǐdá jīchǎng.
example.english: The plane will arrive at the airport at eight in the evening.
example.fact: NASA's New Horizons probe took over nine years to arrive at Pluto after launching in 2006, traveling roughly 4.7 billion kilometers, and its brief flyby in 2015 revealed a heart-shaped glacier of nitrogen ice and mountain ranges made of water ice, features no one had expected from a world once dismissed as a frozen, featureless rock.

examples.hanzi: 我们的火车将在中午十二点抵达北京。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen de huǒchē jiāng zài zhōngwǔ shí'èr diǎn dǐdá Běijīng.
examples.english: Our train will arrive in Beijing at noon.

examples.hanzi: 抵达酒店以后,请给我发个消息。
examples.pinyin: Dǐdá jiǔdiàn yǐhòu, qǐng gěi wǒ fā gè xiāoxi.
examples.english: Please text me once you reach the hotel.

components.note: 南 (nán) — south; as a part it sounds out 楠 nán and 喃 nán.
阝 on the right is 邑 (city) — places, as in 都 capital, 邮 post, 那: a district or ministry.
咅 (pǒu) is a loose sound clue for bù; 咅 also in 剖 pōu, 培 péi and 陪 péi.

example.hanzi: 这种气候在南部地区更为常见。
example.pinyin: zhè zhǒng qìhòu zài nánbù dìqū gèng wéi chángjiàn.
example.english: This type of climate is more common in the southern region.
example.fact: Because Earth is tilted on its axis, the southern hemisphere experiences summer in December and winter in June, exactly opposite the northern hemisphere, and Antarctica in the far south holds about 70 percent of the world's fresh water, locked away as ice.

examples.hanzi: 我家在这个国家的南部,那里很暖和。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā zài zhège guójiā de nánbù, nàlǐ hěn nuǎnhuo.
examples.english: My home is in the southern part of this country, where it's warm.

examples.hanzi: 这个省的南部有很多山。
examples.pinyin: Zhège shěng de nánbù yǒu hěn duō shān.
examples.english: The southern part of this province has many mountains.

components.note: 一 (one) — a single horizontal stroke is the number one; 二 and 三 just add strokes, so the first three numbers are tally marks.
禾 (grain) — 秒 first meant a grain's fine tip; also in 种 plant, 秋 autumn.
少 (shǎo) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 妙 miào and 纱 shā.

example.hanzi: 光在一秒内可以绕地球七圈半。
example.pinyin: guāng zài yī miǎo nèi kěyǐ rào dìqiú qī quān bàn.
example.english: Light can travel around the Earth about seven and a half times in one second.
example.fact: A second is now officially defined not by clocks or the Earth's rotation but by the vibration of a cesium-133 atom, which oscillates exactly 9,192,631,770 times during one second — a definition adopted in 1967 that is so precise modern atomic clocks would lose only about one second every 300 million years.

examples.hanzi: 请再等一秒,我马上就好。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng zài děng yì miǎo, wǒ mǎshàng jiù hǎo.
examples.english: Please wait one more second; I'll be done right away.

examples.hanzi: 他只用了一秒就想出了答案。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhǐ yòngle yì miǎo jiù xiǎngchūle dá'àn.
examples.english: It took him just one second to come up with the answer.

components.note: 手 (hand) — a picture of a hand with fingers spread. As a left-hand radical it becomes 扌 in 打 hit, 拿 take, 推 push.
術 (traditional) — 行 (road) plus 朮 (zhú) as sound: art, method. 术 is the sound part alone; same sound in 述 shù, as in 手术, 技术, 艺术.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 字: a room under the roof.
至 (zhì, arrive) is a loose sound clue for shì; it fits the meaning: where one arrives inside the house.

example.hanzi: 医生正在手术室里为病人做手术。
example.pinyin: yīshēng zhèngzài shǒushùshì lǐ wèi bìngrén zuò shǒushù.
example.english: The doctor is performing surgery on the patient in the operating room.
example.fact: Before general anesthesia became common in the 1840s, surgeons prized speed above all else — the 19th-century Scottish surgeon Robert Liston reportedly could amputate a leg in under 30 seconds, since faster surgery meant less blood loss and less time for a fully conscious patient to suffer or struggle.

examples.hanzi: 病人被推进了手术室。
examples.pinyin: Bìngrén bèi tuījìnle shǒushùshì.
examples.english: The patient was wheeled into the operating room.

examples.hanzi: 手术室的灯一直亮着。
examples.pinyin: Shǒushùshì de dēng yìzhí liàngzhe.
examples.english: The light in the operating room has stayed on.

components.note: 彳 (step) — left half of a crossroads: 行 pictures a crossroads, so to go, and (háng) a row or trade.
日 (sun) — sun, light and time: 明 bright, 晴 clear, 时 time; stars are points of light.
生 (shēng) is a loose sound hint for xīng (-ng ending); also in 性 xìng, 姓 xìng.

example.hanzi: 科学家发现了一颗新的行星。
example.pinyin: kēxuéjiā fāxiàn le yī kē xīn de xíngxīng.
example.english: Scientists discovered a new planet.
example.fact: As of the mid-2020s, astronomers have confirmed over 5,000 exoplanets orbiting other stars, most detected by watching for the tiny dip in a star's brightness as a planet passes in front of it. One of the strangest finds, WASP-76b, is thought to rain molten iron on its permanent night side after temperatures on its scorching day side vaporize metal.

examples.hanzi: 地球是太阳系中的一颗行星。
examples.pinyin: Dìqiú shì tàiyángxì zhōng de yì kē xíngxīng.
examples.english: The Earth is a planet in the solar system.

examples.hanzi: 你知道离太阳最近的行星是哪一颗吗?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhīdào lí tàiyáng zuì jìn de xíngxīng shì nǎ yì kē ma?
examples.english: Do you know which planet is closest to the sun?

components.note: 月 (flesh/meat, not moon here) — oldest form is a hand holding a piece of meat, "to possess"; 月 as meat also appears in 肉 words like 肚 belly and 脑 brain.
力 (strength) — an old picture of an arm or a plough, a tool of effort. As a radical it marks strength: 办, 助, 动, 努, 男.

example.hanzi: 这个证据非常有力，足以证明他的清白。
example.pinyin: zhège zhèngjù fēicháng yǒulì, zúyǐ zhèngmíng tā de qīngbái.
example.english: This evidence is very compelling, enough to prove his innocence.
example.fact: DNA fingerprinting was first used to solve a criminal case in 1986 in England, when British geneticist Alec Jeffreys's technique both convicted a killer and exonerated a wrongly suspected man, launching forensic DNA analysis as one of the most powerful tools in modern criminal investigation.

examples.hanzi: 他的声音很有力,大家都听得很清楚。
examples.pinyin: Tā de shēngyīn hěn yǒulì, dàjiā dōu tīng de hěn qīngchu.
examples.english: His voice is strong, and everyone can hear him clearly.

examples.hanzi: 这位运动员的手臂特别有力。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi yùndòngyuán de shǒubì tèbié yǒulì.
examples.english: This athlete's arms are especially powerful.

components.note: 贝 (shell, money) — 贝 is the money radical — 财, 贵, 买, 费; betting stakes money.
者 (zhě) — near hint — 赌 is dǔ; 者 also sounds out 堵 dǔ and 都 dū.
氵 (water) — water and pouring, as in 河, 海, 清: 注 is to pour in.
主 (zhǔ) is a close sound clue for zhù; 主 also in 住 zhù, 柱 zhù and 驻 zhù.

example.hanzi: 他在这次投资中下了很大的赌注。
example.pinyin: tā zài zhè cì tóuzī zhōng xiàle hěn dà de dǔzhù.
example.english: He put down a huge stake in this investment.
example.fact: In 1956, Nathan Detroit-style casino math aside, real gambling odds are precisely calculable: the house edge in roulette comes from the single extra zero pocket, giving the casino a mathematical advantage of about 2.7 percent on every spin regardless of how players bet, a built-in edge that guarantees long-run profit for the house.

examples.hanzi: 他们拿钱当赌注,打赌谁会赢。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen ná qián dāng dǔzhù, dǎdǔ shéi huì yíng.
examples.english: They put money on it as a stake and bet on who would win.

examples.hanzi: 这场比赛的赌注是一顿晚饭。
examples.pinyin: Zhè chǎng bǐsài de dǔzhù shì yí dùn wǎnfàn.
examples.english: The stake of this contest is a dinner.

components.note: 一 (one) — a single horizontal stroke is the number one; 二 and 三 just add strokes, so the first three numbers are tally marks.
氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 海, 汤; 流 is flowing water.
㐬 (liú) — same sound — 流 is liú; 㐬 also sounds out 琉 liú and 硫 liú.

example.hanzi: 这家餐厅的服务是一流的。
example.pinyin: zhè jiā cāntīng de fúwù shì yīliú de.
example.english: This restaurant's service is top quality.
example.fact: Switzerland has topped global innovation and competitiveness rankings for years running, a position researchers link to its dense concentration of research institutions like ETH Zurich, its strong vocational-training system, and one of the world's highest rates of patents filed per capita.

examples.hanzi: 这家酒店的设备是一流的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā jiǔdiàn de shèbèi shì yīliú de.
examples.english: This hotel's equipment is first-rate.

examples.hanzi: 他的足球水平在全国是一流的。
examples.pinyin: Tā de zúqiú shuǐpíng zài quánguó shì yīliú de.
examples.english: His soccer skill is among the best in the country.

components.note: 王 (jade, 斜玉旁) — precious gems, as in 球 ball, 珠 pearl, 玩 play.
㐱 (zhěn, the right part 人彡) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 诊 zhěn and 疹 zhěn.
忄 (heart) — 忄 is the heart radical for feelings, as in 情, 怕; 惜 is the feeling of cherishing.
昔 (xī) — same sound — 惜 is xī, like 昔 (in the past); 昔 also sounds out 借 jiè and 错 cuò.

example.hanzi: 我们应该珍惜和家人相处的时光。
example.pinyin: wǒmen yīnggāi zhēnxī hé jiārén xiāngchǔ de shíguāng.
example.english: We should cherish the time spent with family.
example.fact: Giant pandas spend up to 14 hours a day eating bamboo just to meet their energy needs, since bamboo is so low in nutrients, yet conservation efforts since the 1980s have helped move the species from endangered to vulnerable status by 2016, one of the rare modern success stories in wildlife protection.

examples.hanzi: 这是爷爷留下的旧表,我很珍惜。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yéye liúxià de jiù biǎo, wǒ hěn zhēnxī.
examples.english: This old watch was left by my grandfather, and I cherish it.

examples.hanzi: 你要珍惜每一次学习的机会。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yào zhēnxī měi yí cì xuéxí de jīhuì.
examples.english: You should value every chance to learn.

components.note: 成 (chéng) is a sound clue for 城 chéng, 诚 chéng and 盛 chéng: the same sound.
木 (tree) — trees and wood, as in 树 tree, 林 woods, 桌 table; the fruit hangs on the tree.
田 (field) here is the round fruit drawn on the tree. 果 also gives the sound for 课 kè and 颗 kē.

example.hanzi: 这项研究的成果得到了广泛认可。
example.pinyin: zhè xiàng yánjiū de chéngguǒ dédàole guǎngfàn rènkě.
example.english: The results of this research have been widely recognized.
example.fact: Penicillin, discovered by Alexander Fleming in 1928 after he noticed mold had killed bacteria in a forgotten petri dish, was not turned into a usable medicine until over a decade later, when a team led by Howard Florey and Ernst Chain developed methods to mass-produce it in time to treat wounded soldiers during World War II.

examples.hanzi: 这次实验取得了很好的成果。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì shíyàn qǔdéle hěn hǎo de chéngguǒ.
examples.english: This experiment achieved great results.

examples.hanzi: 这是大家辛苦工作的成果。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì dàjiā xīnkǔ gōngzuò de chéngguǒ.
examples.english: This is the fruit of everyone's hard work.

components.note: 土 (earth) — banking up soil around plants; also in 地 ground, 城 city.
咅 (pōu) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 陪 péi and 赔 péi.
羊 (yáng) hints at the sound: 养 yǎng is close, as in 样 yàng and 洋 yáng; the old form 養 added 食 food.

example.hanzi: 老师鼓励学生从小培养阅读的习惯。
example.pinyin: lǎoshī gǔlì xuéshēng cóngxiǎo péiyǎng yuèdú de xíguàn.
example.english: Teachers encourage students to cultivate a reading habit from a young age.
example.fact: Petri dishes, invented by German bacteriologist Julius Richard Petri in 1887 while working in Robert Koch's laboratory, remain the standard tool for culturing microorganisms over 130 years later, and the agar gel typically used inside them is derived from red algae, a substance first adopted for lab use in 19th-century Japan.

examples.hanzi: 父母要培养孩子的好习惯。
examples.pinyin: Fùmǔ yào péiyǎng háizi de hǎo xíguàn.
examples.english: Parents should cultivate good habits in their children.

examples.hanzi: 这所学校培养了很多优秀的人才。
examples.pinyin: Zhè suǒ xuéxiào péiyǎngle hěn duō yōuxiù de réncái.
examples.english: This school has trained many outstanding people.

components.note: 周 (zhōu) also lends its sound to 调 diào/tiáo, 稠 chóu, 绸 chóu and 凋 diāo.
囗 (enclosure) — the outer box, as in 国 country and 回. The dictionary reading: four walls of a room, with a child (儿) inside; memory aid only, sound-borrowed.
儿 (legs/child) — inside the box, as in 先 and 兄. Memory aid: the shape is simply a box with two legs; it does not explain 'four'.

example.hanzi: 我们周四下午有一场重要的会议。
example.pinyin: wǒmen zhōusì xiàwǔ yǒu yī chǎng zhòngyào de huìyì.
example.english: We have an important meeting on Thursday afternoon.
example.fact: Thursday is named after Thor, the Norse god of thunder, via the Old English 'Thunresdæg,' mirroring how the Romans named the same day after Jupiter, their own thunder god — a naming pattern found across many European languages that mapped their gods onto the Roman planetary week.

examples.hanzi: 周四我要去看牙医。
examples.pinyin: Zhōusì wǒ yào qù kàn yáyī.
examples.english: I'm going to see the dentist on Thursday.

examples.hanzi: 我们每周四晚上都在一起打篮球。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen měi zhōusì wǎnshang dōu zài yìqǐ dǎ lánqiú.
examples.english: We play basketball together every Thursday evening.

components.note: 儿 (legs, person) — with a foot 𠂉 above: a foot stepping out in front of a person, so "first, earlier".
口 (mouth) — knowing is something you can say aloud; 口 sits in many speech words (问 ask, 告 tell).
矢 (shǐ, arrow) is only a loose sound clue today; the same 知 sound is in 智 zhì (wisdom).

example.hanzi: 古代的先知常常预言未来的灾难。
example.pinyin: gǔdài de xiānzhī chángcháng yùyán wèilái de zāinàn.
example.english: Ancient prophets often foretold future disasters.
example.fact: The Oracle of Delphi in ancient Greece was consulted by kings and commoners alike for centuries, and modern geological studies suggest the priestess's trance-like prophecies may have been influenced by ethylene or other gases seeping up through a fault line beneath the temple, offering a scientific explanation for an ancient religious phenomenon.

examples.hanzi: 这位先知在故事里提前知道了结局。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi xiānzhī zài gùshi lǐ tíqián zhīdàole jiéjú.
examples.english: In the story, this prophet knew the ending in advance.

examples.hanzi: 他像先知一样,早就预料到了这件事。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiàng xiānzhī yíyàng, zǎojiù yùliàodàole zhè jiàn shì.
examples.english: Like a seer, he foresaw this long ago.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — neatly stacked crops, hence order; also in 种 plant, 秋 autumn.
失 (shī) is only a loose sound clue for zhì.
广 (building) — 广 is a building or wide roof, as in 店 shop, 床 bed, 库 store; 序 is order and sequence.
予 (yǔ) — near sound — 序 is xù; 予 also sounds out 预 yù and 野 yě.

example.hanzi: 维持社会秩序是政府的重要职责。
example.pinyin: wéichí shèhuì zhìxù shì zhèngfǔ de zhòngyào zhízé.
example.english: Maintaining social order is an important responsibility of the government.
example.fact: Ant colonies maintain remarkably strict order without any central leader, coordinating tens of thousands of workers through pheromone trails alone. Studies of ant traffic have found they self-organize to avoid congestion so efficiently that engineers have borrowed their algorithms to improve computer network routing and truck logistics.

examples.hanzi: 排队的时候要遵守秩序。
examples.pinyin: Páiduì de shíhou yào zūnshǒu zhìxù.
examples.english: You have to follow order when queuing.

examples.hanzi: 警察正在路口维持交通秩序。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá zhèngzài lùkǒu wéichí jiāotōng zhìxù.
examples.english: The police are maintaining traffic order at the intersection.

components.note: 田 (field) — a field above 力 (strength): a man is one who works the fields with strength.
士 (scholar, soldier) — usually read as an axe or weapon, so a warrior or gentleman (士兵, 博士). Memory aid: 士 has the longer bar on top, 土 (earth) on the bottom.

example.hanzi: 这家理发店专门为男士提供服务。
example.pinyin: zhè jiā lǐfàdiàn zhuānmén wèi nánshì tígōng fúwù.
example.english: This barbershop specializes in serving men.
example.fact: The necktie is believed to trace back to Croatian mercenaries serving in France in the 17th century, whose neck scarves caught the eye of French nobility and were adapted into the 'cravat,' the direct ancestor of the modern tie still worn by men in business attire today.

examples.hanzi: 这位男士,请问您需要帮忙吗?
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi nánshì, qǐngwèn nín xūyào bāngmáng ma?
examples.english: Sir, do you need any help?

examples.hanzi: 商场三楼是男士服装区。
examples.pinyin: Shāngchǎng sān lóu shì nánshì fúzhuāng qū.
examples.english: The third floor of the mall is the men's clothing section.

components.note: 彡 (patterns, hairlines) — marks shape, shadow and decoration, as in 影 shadow, 彩 colour; 形 is a shape.
开 (a worn-down 幵) hints at the sound: 形 xíng sounds like 刑 and 型.
犬 (dog) — animals: 狗, 猫; 状 first meant the shape of an animal.
丬 (a form of 爿) gives zhuàng: also in 壮 zhuàng, 装 zhuāng, 将 jiāng and 奖 jiǎng.

example.hanzi: 这块石头的形状很奇特。
example.pinyin: zhè kuài shítou de xíngzhuàng hěn qítè.
example.english: This stone has a very peculiar shape.
example.fact: Honeycomb cells form hexagons not because bees deliberately choose that shape but because wax naturally settles into hexagons under the physical pressures of surface tension and crowding, the same geometric principle mathematicians proved in the 'honeycomb conjecture' minimizes the material needed to enclose a given amount of space.

examples.hanzi: 这个盒子的形状像一颗心。
examples.pinyin: Zhège hézi de xíngzhuàng xiàng yì kē xīn.
examples.english: This box is shaped like a heart.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们用泥巴捏出了各种形状。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen yòng níbā niēchūle gèzhǒng xíngzhuàng.
examples.english: The children molded all kinds of shapes with clay.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 拿, 抱, 把; 打 is to hit.
丁 (dīng) is a loose sound clue for dǎ; 丁 also sounds out 订 dìng, 顶 dǐng and 钉 dīng.
亻 (person) — a person falling over; marks people and their actions, as in 你, 做.
到 (dào) gives the sound: 倒 is dǎo (fall) or dào (upside down).

example.hanzi: 示威者高呼口号，要求打倒腐败官员。
example.pinyin: shìwēizhě gāohū kǒuhào, yāoqiú dǎdǎo fǔbài guānyuán.
example.english: The protesters shouted slogans, demanding the overthrow of corrupt officials.
example.fact: The fall of the Berlin Wall in November 1989 began almost by accident, when an East German official misspoke at a press conference and implied border crossings were opening immediately; crowds rushed the checkpoints that same night, and guards, lacking clear orders, simply let them through.

examples.hanzi: 他一拳就把对手打倒了。
examples.pinyin: Tā yì quán jiù bǎ duìshǒu dǎdǎo le.
examples.english: He knocked his opponent down with one punch.

examples.hanzi: 我们必须打倒懒惰,才能取得进步。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen bìxū dǎdǎo lǎnduò, cái néng qǔdé jìnbù.
examples.english: We must defeat laziness in order to make progress.

components.note: 犭 (animal, 反犬旁) — beasts and hunting dogs, as in 狗 dog, 猫 cat, 狼 wolf.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 这位猎人在森林里追踪野兔的足迹。
example.pinyin: zhè wèi lièrén zài sēnlín lǐ zhuīzōng yětù de zújì.
example.english: This hunter tracked the wild rabbit's footprints in the forest.
example.fact: The San people of the Kalahari Desert practice persistence hunting, chasing an animal like a kudu for hours under the midday sun until it collapses from heatstroke, since humans can dissipate heat through sweating far more efficiently than most four-legged prey, a trait some scientists argue shaped early human evolution.

examples.hanzi: 这个猎人每年冬天都进山打猎。
examples.pinyin: Zhège lièrén měi nián dōngtiān dōu jìn shān dǎliè.
examples.english: This hunter goes into the mountains to hunt every winter.

examples.hanzi: 故事里的猎人救了小红帽。
examples.pinyin: Gùshi lǐ de lièrén jiùle Xiǎohóngmào.
examples.english: In the story, the hunter saved Little Red Riding Hood.

components.note: 钅 (metal; traditional 金) — marks metals, as in 钱 money, 铁 iron, 铜 copper; 锅 is a pot or pan.
呙 (guō) — same sound: 锅 guō. 呙 also sounds out 蜗 wō and 窝 wō.

example.hanzi: 妈妈用锅煮汤。
example.pinyin: Māma yòng guō zhǔ tāng.
example.english: Mom is cooking soup in the pot.
example.fact: 锅 covers pots and woks: 炒锅 (wok), 火锅 (hot pot), 电饭锅 (rice cooker), 压力锅. In slang, 背锅 means to take the blame, literally "carry the pot," and 甩锅 means to shift it onto someone else.

examples.hanzi: 这口锅太大了，我们用不着。
examples.pinyin: Zhè kǒu guō tài dà le, wǒmen yòng bu zháo.
examples.english: This pot is too big, and I will not need it.

examples.hanzi: 今晚我们去吃火锅吧。
examples.pinyin: Jīnwǎn wǒmen qù chī huǒguō ba.
examples.english: Let's go have hot pot tonight.

components.note: 心 (heart) — 心 marks feelings, as in 想, 爱, 怒; 悲 is sorrow.
非 (fēi) — near sound — 悲 is bēi; 非 also sounds out 辈 bèi and 排 pái.
口 (mouth) — a cry of sorrow; also in 叫 shout, 哭 weep.
衣 (yī) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 依 yī.

example.hanzi: 失去亲人让他感到无比悲哀。
example.pinyin: shīqù qīnrén ràng tā gǎndào wúbǐ bēiāi.
example.english: Losing his loved one made him feel immensely sorrowful.
example.fact: Elephants are among the few non-human animals observed engaging in what researchers call grieving behavior, standing over and touching the bones of dead herd members for extended periods, and some matriarchs have been seen returning to the same site years after a death, long after the bones have weathered away.

examples.hanzi: 这部电影的结局让人觉得很悲哀。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng de jiéjú ràng rén juéde hěn bēi'āi.
examples.english: The ending of this movie feels very sad.

examples.hanzi: 他悲哀地看着空荡荡的房间。
examples.pinyin: Tā bēi'āi de kànzhe kōngdàngdàng de fángjiān.
examples.english: He gazed sadly at the empty room.

components.note: 中 (middle) — a line through the middle of a box, a centre mark. 中 gives sound to 钟 zhōng, 种 zhǒng, 忠 zhōng and 衷 zhōng.
龶 (plant-like top) — dictionary reads the top as 'a poisonous plant'. Memory aid: a plant growing on top of a mother (母) is something you must not eat.
母 (mǔ, mother) — the bottom part and radical. Sound clue is lost today (毒 is dú); use it as a visual memory aid, as in 母亲.

example.hanzi: 他因为吃了变质的食物而食物中毒。
example.pinyin: tā yīnwèi chīle biànzhí de shíwù ér shíwù zhòngdú.
example.english: He got food poisoning from eating spoiled food.
example.fact: Botulinum toxin, the substance behind botulism poisoning, is considered one of the most lethal natural substances known, with an estimated lethal dose for humans measured in mere nanograms — yet heavily diluted medical versions of the same toxin are used safely worldwide as Botox to relax muscles and smooth wrinkles.

examples.hanzi: 他吃了坏掉的蘑菇,中毒进了医院。
examples.pinyin: Tā chīle huàidiào de mógu, zhòngdú jìnle yīyuàn.
examples.english: He ate spoiled mushrooms, got poisoned and went to the hospital.

examples.hanzi: 炉子漏气会让人煤气中毒。
examples.pinyin: Lúzi lòuqì huì ràng rén méiqì zhòngdú.
examples.english: A leaking stove can cause gas poisoning.

components.note: 发 (send out, hair) — two characters merged in simplified writing: 發 fā "emit, issue" and 髮 fà "hair" (头发).
见 (see) — seeing and perceiving, as in 现, 看, 视: 觉 is to sense and become aware (jué), also "sleep" (jiào) in 睡觉.
The top is a shape of 学 (xué), a loose sound hint from the traditional 覺.

example.hanzi: 她突然发觉自己把钱包忘在家里了。
example.pinyin: tā tūrán fājué zìjǐ bǎ qiánbāo wàng zài jiālǐ le.
example.english: She suddenly realized she had left her wallet at home.
example.fact: Alexander Fleming's discovery of penicillin's antibacterial power in 1928 happened only because he noticed, almost by chance, that a stray mold spore had drifted into an uncovered petri dish and killed the bacteria growing around it — a moment of realization now considered one of the most important accidents in medical history.

examples.hanzi: 我走到门口才发觉下雨了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zǒudào ménkǒu cái fājué xiàyǔ le.
examples.english: I only realized it was raining when I reached the door.

examples.hanzi: 他发觉有人一直在跟着他。
examples.pinyin: Tā fājué yǒu rén yìzhí zài gēnzhe tā.
examples.english: He noticed someone had been following him.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — crops: 秋 autumn, 种 plant, 秒 second; 私 was grain held for oneself.
厶 (sī) is the ancient form of 私 itself, meaning private; 公 gōng (public) is its opposite.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 室 room, 安 safe, 字 character; 家 is home.
豕 (pig) — a pig under a roof: pigs were kept in the home, hence home and family.

example.hanzi: 这条路是私家车道，禁止停车。
example.pinyin: zhè tiáo lù shì sījiā chēdào, jìnzhǐ tíngchē.
example.english: This road is a private driveway; parking is prohibited.
example.fact: Venice has no private cars at all within its historic center, since the city is built across more than 100 small islands linked by canals and roughly 400 bridges, making boats — including private motorboats owned by wealthier residents — the only practical form of personal transport.

examples.hanzi: 他们家有一个私家花园。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen jiā yǒu yí gè sījiā huāyuán.
examples.english: Their home has a private garden.

examples.hanzi: 这条小路是私家路,别进去。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo xiǎolù shì sījiā lù, bié jìnqù.
examples.english: This small road is private; don't go in.

components.note: 攵 (tap, strike) — hand holding a stick, as in 教 teach, 收 collect, 放 release: correcting by hand.
己 (jǐ) is a close sound clue for gǎi.
辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过, 进, 送; 造 is to go and make something.
告 (gào) is a loose sound clue (-ao); also in 浩 hào, 靠 kào.

example.hanzi: 政府计划改造这片老旧的城区。
example.pinyin: zhèngfǔ jìhuà gǎizào zhè piàn lǎojiù de chéngqū.
example.english: The government plans to redevelop this old district.
example.fact: The Netherlands has reclaimed roughly 17 percent of its current land area from the sea and lakes using a system of dikes, pumps, and windmills developed over centuries, transforming what was once shallow water into the polders that now hold major cities and farmland below sea level.

examples.hanzi: 我们打算改造这间旧厨房。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen dǎsuàn gǎizào zhè jiān jiù chúfáng.
examples.english: We're planning to remodel this old kitchen.

examples.hanzi: 这家工厂经过改造以后效率提高了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngchǎng jīngguò gǎizào yǐhòu xiàolǜ tígāo le.
examples.english: After being renovated, this factory has become more efficient.

components.note: 矢 (arrow) — the arrow was an ancient measure; also in 知 know, 矮 short, 射 shoot.
豆 (dòu) is only a loose sound clue for duǎn.
衤 (clothing, 衣字旁) — clothes: 衬 shirt, 衫, 裙 skirt, 被 quilt; 裤 is trousers.
库 (kù) sounds exactly like 裤.

example.hanzi: 夏天的时候，他总是穿短裤出门。
example.pinyin: xiàtiān de shíhou, tā zǒngshì chuān duǎnkù chūmén.
example.english: In summer, he always goes out wearing shorts.
example.fact: Denim, the fabric behind blue jeans and many shorts, was originally developed in the French city of Nîmes, and its name is thought to derive from 'serge de Nîmes.' The indigo dye traditionally used to color it comes from a plant whose pigment must be chemically transformed through oxidation to turn from yellow-green to the familiar deep blue only after the fabric is exposed to air.

examples.hanzi: 这条短裤太短了,我不好意思穿。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo duǎnkù tài duǎn le, wǒ bù hǎoyìsi chuān.
examples.english: These shorts are too short and I'm embarrassed to wear them.

examples.hanzi: 他穿着短裤和拖鞋去海边。
examples.pinyin: Tā chuānzhe duǎnkù hé tuōxié qù hǎibiān.
examples.english: He wore shorts and sandals to the beach.

components.note: 足 (foot) — 足 (⻊ on the left) is the foot radical, as in 跳 jump, 路 road, 踢 kick; 跑 is to run.
包 (bāo) — near sound — 跑 is pǎo; 包 also sounds out 抱 bào, 饱 bǎo and 泡 pào.
止 (foot) — two footprints, one above the other, make a step; the same 止 is in 走 walk and 跑 run.

example.hanzi: 他每天早上坚持跑步一个小时。
example.pinyin: tā měitiān zǎoshang jiānchí pǎobù yī gè xiǎoshí.
example.english: He insists on running for an hour every morning.
example.fact: Kenyan long-distance runners, particularly from the Kalenjin ethnic group, have dominated world marathon rankings for decades, and researchers studying the phenomenon point to a combination of factors including training at high altitude around 2,000 meters, which boosts oxygen-carrying red blood cells, along with a culture that has long emphasized running as transportation and sport from childhood.

examples.hanzi: 我们每天晚上在公园跑步。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen měitiān wǎnshang zài gōngyuán pǎobù.
examples.english: We jog in the park every evening.

examples.hanzi: 下雨天不能出去,只好在家里的跑步机上跑步。
examples.pinyin: Xiàyǔ tiān bù néng chūqù, zhǐhǎo zài jiālǐ de pǎobùjī shàng pǎobù.
examples.english: On rainy days we can't go out, so we have to run on the treadmill at home.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 傻 is a foolish person.
彐 (hand-like part) — 事 is usually explained as a hand holding a tool or tally, 'handling business' — a hedged reading, not certain.
史 (history, scribe) — shares an ancient root with 事: a hand holding a recording tool. Both are about handling official 'matters'.

example.hanzi: 他年轻的时候做过不少傻事。
example.pinyin: tā niánqīng de shíhou zuòguò bùshǎo shǎshì.
example.english: He did quite a few foolish things when he was young.
example.fact: The Darwin Awards, an informal internet tradition started in the early 1990s, humorously chronicled real cases of people who died or were sterilized through spectacularly foolish self-inflicted accidents, framed as a tongue-in-cheek nod to natural selection removing certain behaviors from the gene pool.

examples.hanzi: 我小时候干过一件傻事,到现在还记得。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎoshíhou gànguo yí jiàn shǎshì, dào xiànzài hái jìde.
examples.english: I did something silly as a child that I still remember.

examples.hanzi: 别做傻事,冷静一点。
examples.pinyin: Bié zuò shǎshì, lěngjìng yìdiǎn.
examples.english: Don't do anything foolish; calm down.

components.note: 艹 (grass, plants) — 艹 marks plants — 艺 originally meant planting and cultivating, later skill and art.
乙 (yǐ) — near sound — 艺 is yì, same syllable with another tone.

example.hanzi: 他有一门好手艺。
example.pinyin: Tā yǒu yì mén hǎo shǒuyì.
example.english: He has a good craft skill.
example.fact: 艺 originally meant planting, which is why it has the grass radical, and later grew to "skill." It builds 艺术 (art), 手艺 (craftsmanship), 才艺 (talent), 园艺 (gardening) and 工艺 (craft).

examples.hanzi: 这位老师傅的手艺很好。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi lǎo shīfu de shǒuyì hěn hǎo.
examples.english: This old master has excellent craftsmanship.

examples.hanzi: 她从小就喜欢艺术。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóngxiǎo jiù xǐhuan yìshù.
examples.english: She has liked art since childhood.

components.note: 石 (stone) — marks stones and minerals, as in 碎 shatter, 破 break, 磨 grind; 砰 imitates a bang, like stones striking.
平 (píng) — close sound: 砰 pēng. 平 also sounds out 苹 píng and 评 píng.

example.hanzi: 门砰的一声关上了。
example.pinyin: Mén pēng de yì shēng guān shàng le.
example.english: The door shut with a bang.
example.fact: 砰 imitates a loud bang. 砰的一声 means "with a bang." 砰砰 can also describe a heart pounding: 心砰砰跳. Compare 乒乓 (pīngpāng), the sound of table tennis.

examples.hanzi: 窗户被风吹得砰砰响。
examples.pinyin: Chuānghu bèi fēng chuī de pēngpēng xiǎng.
examples.english: The windows are banging in the wind.

examples.hanzi: 他砰地把房门关上了。
examples.pinyin: Tā pēng de bǎ fángmén guānshàng le.
examples.english: He slammed the door with a bang.

components.note: 土 (earth) — marks soil and ground, as in 地 ground, 城 city wall, 坏 broken; 坑 is a pit dug in the ground.
亢 (kàng) — close sound: 坑 kēng. 亢 also sounds out 抗 kàng and 航 háng.

example.hanzi: 路上有一个很大的坑。
example.pinyin: Lù shàng yǒu yí ge hěn dà de kēng.
example.english: There is a huge pit in the road.
example.fact: 坑 is a hole: 水坑 (puddle), 坑洼 (bumpy). It is slang for a scam: 被坑了 (got ripped off), 坑人 (to cheat people). 萝卜坑, a "radish hole," describes a position that is already taken.

examples.hanzi: 地上有一个很深的坑。
examples.pinyin: Dìshàng yǒu yí ge hěn shēn de kēng.
examples.english: There is a very deep pit in the ground.

examples.hanzi: 这家店的价格太坑人了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de jiàgé tài kēngrén le.
examples.english: The prices at this shop are a rip-off.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — presenting in words; also in 叫 shout, 问 ask. 呈 also sounds out 程 chéng and 逞 chěng.

example.hanzi: 湖水呈现出美丽的蓝色。
example.pinyin: Húshuǐ chéngxiàn chū měilì de lánsè.
example.english: The lake appears a beautiful blue.
example.fact: 呈 means to present or to appear in a form: 呈现 (to show), 呈上 (to hand up), 呈报 (to report to a superior). 呈 plus a shape or color describes appearance, as in 呈圆形 (round in shape).

examples.hanzi: 这座山呈圆锥形。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò shān chéng yuánzhuīxíng.
examples.english: This mountain is cone-shaped.

examples.hanzi: 他把报告呈给了经理。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ bàogào chéng gěi le jīnglǐ.
examples.english: He submitted the report to the manager.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 傲 is a proud person.
敖 (áo) is a near sound match for ào; also in 熬 áo.
忄 (heart, 竖心旁) — feelings and mind: 怕, 情, 快; 慢 is a slow, unhurried heart.
曼 (màn) sounds exactly like 慢; also in 漫 màn.

example.hanzi: 他的傲慢态度让很多同事感到不满。
example.pinyin: tā de àomàn tàidù ràng hěn duō tóngshì gǎndào bùmǎn.
example.english: His arrogant attitude made many colleagues unhappy.
example.fact: The Titanic was marketed before its 1912 maiden voyage as practically unsinkable, and this widely reported overconfidence is often cited alongside the ship's insufficient lifeboats and its captain's decision to maintain high speed through iceberg-laden waters as compounding factors in the disaster that killed over 1,500 people.

examples.hanzi: 你这样傲慢,没有人会喜欢你。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhèyàng àomàn, méiyǒu rén huì xǐhuan nǐ.
examples.english: If you're this arrogant, nobody will like you.

examples.hanzi: 成功以后,他变得越来越傲慢了。
examples.pinyin: Chénggōng yǐhòu, tā biàn de yuè lái yuè àomàn le.
examples.english: After succeeding, he became more and more arrogant.

components.note: 页 (head, page) — in traditional 頭 (豆 + 页): 页 is an old picture of a head, as in 顶, 领, 额. 头 dropped both parts.
大 (big) — the bottom. Memory aid: a big 大 body with two dots ⺀ like eyes above — the head, as in 头发. The dictionary's reading is loose.
口 (mouth) — speaking, shouting: 叫, 吗, 喊; 号 is to call out, then a call-sign or number.
丂 (kǎo) is only a loose clue; it also appears in 考 kǎo and 巧 qiǎo.

example.hanzi: 他是公司里的头号员工。
example.pinyin: tā shì gōngsī lǐ de tóuhào yuángōng.
example.english: He is the top-ranked employee in the company.
example.fact: Mount Everest, straddling the border between Nepal and Tibet, holds the top rank among Earth's peaks at 8,849 meters — its height was last officially remeasured by a joint Chinese-Nepali survey in 2020, using GPS and gravity data instead of the purely trigonometric methods used a century earlier.

examples.hanzi: 这次考试最大的头号难题是最后一道大题。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì kǎoshì zuì dà de tóuhào nántí shì zuìhòu yí dào dàtí.
examples.english: The number one challenge of this exam was the last big question.

examples.hanzi: 她是我们学校的头号球迷。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì wǒmen xuéxiào de tóuhào qiúmí.
examples.english: She is our school's number one fan.

components.note: 衣 (clothing) — clothes and wear: 衬, 被, 袋; 装 is dress, then to pretend or to load.
壮 (zhuàng) is a near sound match for zhuāng; also in 状 zhuàng and 妆 zhuāng.
彡 (decorative strokes) — marks patterns and adornment, as in 形 shape, 影 shadow, 彩 colour; 修 is to tidy and decorate, then repair.
攸 (yōu) is only a loose hint for xiū; 悠 yōu shares it.

example.hanzi: 他们打算重新装修厨房。
example.pinyin: tāmen dǎsuàn chóngxīn zhuāngxiū chúfáng.
example.english: They plan to renovate the kitchen.
example.fact: Antoni Gaudí's Sagrada Família in Barcelona has been under construction since 1882 and remains unfinished — architects today use 3D-printed models and computer simulations to complete Gaudí's original hand-carved plaster designs, with completion now targeted for the 2030s.

examples.hanzi: 我们下个月要装修新房子。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xià gè yuè yào zhuāngxiū xīn fángzi.
examples.english: We're going to renovate the new house next month.

examples.hanzi: 这家餐厅装修得很有特色。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng zhuāngxiū de hěn yǒu tèsè.
examples.english: This restaurant is decorated in a distinctive style.

components.note: 離 (traditional) — 隹 (bird) plus 离 as sound (lí). 离 was an old name for a mythical beast, so the 'leave' sense comes from 離; 离 kept only the sound part.
土 (earth) — the top part, the ground family as in 地, 场, 块. Memory aid: leave the ground 土 and go off on your own 厶 path.
厶 (private, small loop) — the bottom part. Old forms show a person leaving a place, so the 土 story is only a mnemonic.

example.hanzi: 火车即将离去。
example.pinyin: huǒchē jíjiāng líqù.
example.english: The train is about to leave.
example.fact: The Trans-Siberian Railway, completed in 1916, is the longest railway line in the world at over 9,289 kilometers, connecting Moscow to Vladivostok — a nonstop journey along its full length takes about six days.

examples.hanzi: 他含着眼泪看着妈妈离去。
examples.pinyin: Tā hánzhe yǎnlèi kànzhe māma líqù.
examples.english: He watched his mother leave with tears in his eyes.

examples.hanzi: 一个黑影从窗外离去,没人看见。
examples.pinyin: Yí gè hēiyǐng cóng chuāngwài líqù, méi rén kànjiàn.
examples.english: A dark figure slipped away from outside the window, unseen by anyone.

components.note: 门 (gate) — a picture of a two-leaf door; as a radical it frames characters of doors and openings — 开, 关, 问, 间.
票 (ticket) — originally flames flying up, which is why 票 gives the sound piào/piāo to 漂 and 飘 and biāo to 标; ticket is a later meaning.

example.hanzi: 我买了两张电影门票。
example.pinyin: wǒ mǎi le liǎng zhāng diànyǐng ménpiào.
example.english: I bought two movie tickets.
example.fact: The Lumière brothers held the world's first paid public film screening on December 28, 1895, in the basement of the Grand Café in Paris — admission cost one franc, and the ten short films shown that night reportedly startled early audiences unused to moving pictures.

examples.hanzi: 博物馆的门票是五十元一张。
examples.pinyin: Bówùguǎn de ménpiào shì wǔshí yuán yì zhāng.
examples.english: The museum entrance ticket costs fifty yuan each.

examples.hanzi: 学生凭学生证可以半价买门票。
examples.pinyin: Xuésheng píng xuéshēngzhèng kěyǐ bànjià mǎi ménpiào.
examples.english: Students can buy tickets at half price with a student ID.
